question: us-policy-positions:government-operations.automatic-voter-registration
definition: yes = state law (or, where noted, executive/administrative action) registers eligible people automatically (front-end opt-out or back-end) when they transact with the motor vehicle agency or another state agency, and it is in operation by 2026-01-01; no = registration only on the person's own application (opt-in, including the ordinary motor-voter offer or a mandatory-choice question); North Dakota has no registration and is no.
summarySource: NCSL Automatic Voter Registration summary (2025) and Brennan Center History of AVR & Implementation Dates, checked against state election-office releases (DE 2023, ME 2022, MN 2024, NM 2025, PA 2023, VA 2020) and the Voting Rights Lab tracker; searched 09/2026.

US-AK.note: Approved by 2016 ballot measure (Measure 1); eligible Permanent Fund Dividend applicants are registered with a mailed opt-out notice (back-end), in operation since 2017.

US-AL.note: Not among the states NCSL lists with automatic voter registration; registration is by the person's own application, including the ordinary motor-voter offer.

US-AR.note: Not among the states NCSL lists with automatic voter registration; registration is by the person's own application, including the ordinary motor-voter offer.

US-AZ.note: Not among the states NCSL lists with automatic voter registration; registration is by the person's own application, including the ordinary motor-voter offer.

US-CA.note: California New Motor Voter Program, enacted 2015 and in operation at the DMV since 2018.

US-CO.note: Front-end AVR at the DMV from 2017, converted to back-end AVR (mailed opt-out) in 2020.

US-CT.note: Administrative DMV system from 2016, codified and expanded to other agencies by 2021 law; applicants must decline at the transaction (front-end, hard-stop design).

US-DC.note: Automatic Voter Registration Amendment Act passed by the Council on 11/01/2016; implemented at the DMV.

US-DE.note: Enacted 2021 (back-end at the DMV); in operation from 06/21/2023 for voters not already registered.

US-FL.note: Not among the states NCSL lists with automatic voter registration; registration is by the person's own application, including the ordinary motor-voter offer.

US-GA.note: Adopted administratively (opt-out at the Department of Driver Services) in fall 2016, not by a separate AVR statute.

US-HI.note: Hawaii's 2021 'automatic registration' law registers a license applicant only if the applicant chooses to register on the form (mandatory choice, not opt-out); a 2026 bill (HB 2132) proposed expanding it.

US-IA.note: Not among the states NCSL lists with automatic voter registration; registration is by the person's own application, including the ordinary motor-voter offer.

US-ID.note: Not among AVR states; registration is by the person's own application (Idaho is exempt from the NVRA's motor-voter requirement).

US-IL.note: Signed 08/2017 (unanimous legislature); implemented at the Secretary of State driver facilities and other agencies from 2018.

US-IN.note: Not among the states NCSL lists with automatic voter registration; registration is by the person's own application, including the ordinary motor-voter offer.

US-LA.note: Not among the states NCSL lists with automatic voter registration; registration is by the person's own application, including the ordinary motor-voter offer.

US-MA.note: Enacted 08/2018 and implemented at the RMV and MassHealth from 2020 (back-end with mailed opt-out).

US-MD.note: Secure and Accessible Registration Act signed 04/2018; implemented at the MVA and other agencies.

US-ME.note: Enacted 2019; implemented at the Bureau of Motor Vehicles on 06/21/2022, with the decline offered on the service-window pin pad (front-end).

US-MI.note: Adopted by 2018 ballot Proposal 3 (Mich. Const. art. 2, § 4); implemented at Secretary of State branch offices.

US-MN.note: Enacted 2023; in operation from 04/29/2024, with a 20-day opt-out after processing.

US-MO.note: Not among the states NCSL lists with automatic voter registration; registration is by the person's own application, including the ordinary motor-voter offer.

US-ND.note: North Dakota has no voter registration at all, so there is no automatic registration.

US-NH.note: Not among AVR states; registration is by the person's own application (New Hampshire is exempt from the NVRA's motor-voter requirement).

US-NJ.note: Signed 04/2018; implemented at the Motor Vehicle Commission (front-end opt-out).

US-NM.note: Enacted in the 2023 New Mexico Voting Rights Act (HB 4); AVR at the Motor Vehicle Division took effect 07/01/2025.

US-NV.note: Adopted by 2018 ballot Question 5; back-end AVR at the DMV in operation since 2020.

US-OH.note: Not among the states NCSL lists with automatic voter registration; registration is by the person's own application, including the ordinary motor-voter offer.

US-OR.note: Oregon Motor Voter Act (2015), first state in operation in 2016; back-end with mailed opt-out.

US-PA.note: Executive action, not statute: since 09/2023 PennDOT takes eligible license and ID customers through registration unless they opt out; legislative Republicans dispute the governor's authority.

US-RI.note: Signed by Gov. Raimondo 07/2017; implemented at the Division of Motor Vehicles.

US-SC.note: Not among the states NCSL lists with automatic voter registration; registration is by the person's own application, including the ordinary motor-voter offer.

US-VA.note: 2020 law made DMV registration front-end opt-out; a workgroup has studied moving to back-end AVR.

US-VT.note: Signed 04/2016; in operation at the DMV since 01/01/2017.

US-WA.note: Signed 03/2018; implemented at the Department of Licensing (and Health Benefit Exchange) from 2019.

US-WI.note: Not among AVR states; registration is by the person's own application (Wisconsin's DMV does not offer motor-voter registration because the state is exempt from the NVRA).

US-WV.note: Enacted 04/2016; implementation was repeatedly delayed (statutory deadline 2021) and the front-end opt-out system is now in effect at the DMV; exact start date not found.

US-WY.note: Not among AVR states; registration is by the person's own application (Wyoming is exempt from the NVRA's motor-voter requirement).

unknown.US-NY: Automatic registration (N.Y. Elec. Law § 5-900 et seq., signed 12/2020) was to start 01/2023 but was delayed; the Board of Elections targeted the DMV for early-mid 2025, and no search result confirmed it was operating by 01/01/2026. A pending amendment (S88A) would move the DMV to back-end AVR in 2027.

conflicts.readings: NCSL and several trackers list Hawaii among AVR states; the statute registers a license applicant only if the applicant chooses to register (mandatory choice), which this definition treats as no.
A Brennan Center roundup summary described the DMV as implementing AVR in 01/2023 (the statutory date), while 2024 and 01/2025 reporting said the launch was delayed to 2025 at the earliest.
The governor treats AVR as a procedural PennDOT change within executive authority; legislative Republicans say it required a statute.
